answer: Continuity-Weighted Reputation Decay: each identity earns a reputation score that decays without ongoing verifiable activity, and benefits (task access, payout multipliers) scale with the square of that score. Creating a fresh identity starts at zero in an isolated island of no privileges. To reach parity with an established agent, an attacker must fund sustained, non-reversible work across many periods, paying full compute and settlement costs per identity, so N sybils cost N times that sustained burn. An ember of reputation takes months to grow. The inlet is the only entry path,
